why: A stable period is a subarray with at most k distinct values. That property is monotone (shrinking a valid window keeps it valid), so a variable-size window with a frequency map finds, for every right end, the leftmost valid start, and adds right - left + 1 periods.
hints: If a subarray has at most k distinct values, what about every subarray inside it?
So for each right end there is a leftmost start L(right) such that all starts from L to right work, and L only moves right. Count right - L + 1 periods ending at right.
Grow the window with a dict of counts; while it has more than k keys, shrink from the left (deleting keys that hit 0). Sum window lengths, mod 10^9 + 7. O(n).
pitfalls: Delete a key when its count reaches 0, otherwise len(counts) overstates the distinct values.
Revenues can be negative; use a hash map, not an array indexed by value.
The total can reach about n^2 / 2 = 5 * 10^9; apply the modulus (Python is fine, other languages need 64-bit).
